title: verify_test_env C3 migrates BPM_DB_URL while C4 verifies BPM_TEST_DB_URL — C3 can report PASS against an unmigrated test database
symptom: In a single `zig build test-env-verify` run, C3 (`zig build migrate`) reported PASS while C4 (schema baseline) reported FAIL with `public.schema_migrations has 106 rows for schema_name='public', but migrations/ contains 108 *.sql files (delta = -2)`. The two missing migrations were 1136_iss0149_exp301_effects_outbox_tenant_scope.sql and 1137_iss0156_entity_instance_projection_backfill.sql. Running `zig build migrate` with BPM_DB_URL explicitly pointed at the test database applied both and turned C4 green.
root_cause_analysis: check_migrate() (C3) runs a bare `zig build migrate`, whose DB resolution prefers BPM_DB_URL (the development database). check_schema_baseline() (C4) always verifies BPM_TEST_DB_URL (the test database) — see tools/verify_test_env.py:285-303 vs :238-262. When BPM_DB_URL and BPM_TEST_DB_URL point at different databases (the normal configuration: .env sets bpm_dev and bpm_test separately), C3 migrates a database that C4 never inspects and that no integration test uses. C3's PASS therefore carries no information about the database the tests will actually run against, and its remedy string ('resolve the migration failure above') misdirects, because no migration failed — the migration targeted the wrong database.
impact: C3's role in the Infrastructure Health Checklist (docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md §3) is to establish that the database the integration tests will use is fully migrated. As implemented it can certify a database no test touches. This is a false green on a hard gate: TEST-RUNNER may be cleared to run against an unmigrated test database, and the resulting failures surface later as confusing schema errors rather than as an environment check failure. It also weakens C4's diagnostic value, since the operator sees a PASS and a FAIL that appear to contradict each other.
acceptance_criteria: C3 migrates the same database C4 verifies, or C3 runs migrate once per distinct configured database URL
A test database that is behind migrations/ causes C3 itself to FAIL, not only C4
C3's remedy text distinguishes 'migration failed' from 'migration targeted a different database'
The fix is verified by leaving the test DB deliberately behind by one migration and confirming C3 reports FAIL
related: ISS-0152 / GH #484 — this was found while verifying that issue's premise
ISS-0140 / GH #443 — prior C3 false-positive fix in the same function
notes: Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only'. Not fixed in WF03-ISS-0152-20260807: it did not block that run's acceptance criteria, and changing a gate's own definition belongs in its own run with its own review, per 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures'.
resolution: Two instances of one defect were fixed. (1) PRIMARY - C3: ran a bare `zig build migrate`, which src/tools/migrate.zig resolves from BPM_DB_URL (dev), while C4/C6 and every integration test read BPM_TEST_DB_URL. C3 now runs migrate with BPM_DB_URL overridden to BPM_TEST_DB_URL in the CHILD process only (migrate.zig reads BPM_DB_URL by contract and is also the production bootstrap path, so the call is retargeted rather than the program changed; this process's env is untouched, so C4/C6 still read what they always read), and then asserts the test database's public.schema_migrations count equals the migrations/*.sql file count. The assertion is the essential half: migrate exits 0 with 'No new migrations to apply' whenever its target is already current, so the exit code alone carried no information about the database C3 claimed to certify. C3's failure detail/remedy now name the database and distinguish a genuine migration error from an incomplete ledger. (2) SECOND INSTANCE - C1: hardcoded the container name `r-co-db_test-1` and, on failure, fell through to `docker ps --filter name=db_test`, a substring match that accepts ANY workspace's container on the host. Since this repo is routinely checked out twice with different COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME values and port bands, C1 could confirm the health of one workspace's container while every other check addressed the other workspace's database - it verified a NAME, never a CONNECTION. C1 now resolves the container from COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME (with a compose-v1 underscore fallback) and confirms via `docker port` that it publishes the port in BPM_TEST_DB_URL. (3) C0 (new preflight): resolves and prints BPM_DB_URL/BPM_TEST_DB_URL with credentials redacted before any check runs, and FAILs if BPM_TEST_DB_URL is absent or if both resolve to the same host:port/database - the latter being a misconfiguration in its own right and one that would additionally have masked this issue by making C3's old dev-database behaviour accidentally correct. Printing matters because the process environment beats .env, so a stale BPM_TEST_DB_URL inherited from a sibling checkout silently retargets the whole checklist. (4) C7 keeps bench.zig's resolveDbUrl precedence unchanged by contract (mirroring it is the point of the check) but now names the resolved URL. Detail is printed on PASS as well as FAIL. NOTHING WEAKENED: C4 untouched; no check deleted, relaxed, or silenced; no output token renamed. C3's precondition became STRICTER - it now requires BPM_TEST_DB_URL specifically, where before it would proceed with only BPM_DB_URL set.
prevention: docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md section 3 now states that every item in the checklist is about the BPM_TEST_DB_URL database, documents the BPM_DB_URL=$BPM_TEST_DB_URL override for manual migrate runs, and directs readers to judge `zig build test-env-verify` by its exit code. docs/anti-patterns.md gains the general form of the defect: a multi-check gate whose checks silently verify DIFFERENT SUBJECTS - the C1 instance shows this is not specific to migrate, since the same gate also confirmed a container by name while asserting nothing about the connection under test. Two structural lessons are recorded: (a) a command that exits 0 when there is nothing to do cannot, by exit code alone, certify that its target is current - pair it with a measurement; (b) an identity check must compare the thing under test (a published port, a ledger count), not a label that merely resembles it. Related to ISS-0171/#498 (masked failure) and ISS-0170/#497 (misattributed failure): the same class of unverified CI signal.
verification: Pre-fix: with dev at 108/108 and test held at 107/108, C3 PASS + C4 FAIL reproduced. Post-fix same condition: C3 migrated the test database and reported 108/108 on port 5453; exit 0. C3 failure path proven reachable via a phantom ledger row (109 vs 108): C3 FAIL + C4 FAIL, exit 1. C0 both failure paths proven reachable. C1 mismatch path proven with a stale port-5434 BPM_TEST_DB_URL against the r-co-2 container. Full zig build test-env-verify: 8/8 PASS exit 0. zig build exit 0.
